newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks continue gains, set fresh high.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks continue gains, set fresh high.

text.p: Swiss shares recovered from a weaker start to post a fourth-straight record close.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) closed at 5,141.7 points, up 7.4 points, or 0.14 percent, from Wednesday's close.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was up 6.24 points, or 0.19 percent, to 3,245.92.
"Sell in May and go away does not seem to apply here," one dealer said, adding Swiss shares moved up after an early correction as U.S. bonds rose on latest U.S. data.
"Wall Street seems to be in for another rise, so the prospects are good" for Switzerland, the dealer said.
Bourse turnover was 2.71 billion Swiss francs, at the upper end of average volume.
Most-traded UBS registereds continued their recent strong performance, adding 27 francs to 1,493 on the back of switches from SBC and CS Group.

SBC was favoured by news of plans to buy U.S. investment bank Dillon Read for approximately $600 million. Analysts hailed the move, saying SBC will be able to round out its global investment bank business with the purchase.
Winterthur slumped eight francs to 1,120 on Thursday. It said Wednesday group profit 1996 rose by 21 percent.
One dealer said Winterthur's results failed to top market expectations, unlike those of competitors Swiss Re and Zurich.

Novartis slid 11 francs to 2,028 on profit-taking, while Roche certificates jumped 220 francs to 13,200. The stock profited from news the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's advisory panel recommended the approval of Roche's weight loss drug Xenical. The decision was seen as important given high research and development costs for the drug, one dealer said.
Share prices of Alusuisse, Nestle, SMH, Ciba and Clariant declined.

Swissair lost 40 francs to end at 1,328 francs. Traders said it may have been pressured by the announcement that several competitors, including German Lufthansa are to establish closer ties under the name of Star Alliance.
"But I think Swissair will be able to face the challenge," one dealer said, noting a loss or 40 francs was not exceptional for the stock.
On the Swiss Options and Financial Futures Exchange (Soffex), trade concentrated on SMI futures ahead of Friday's Soffex expiry.
